findings.claim: The gitlink bump rewrites the event emitters of five intelligence workers that are not in the touch-point list (chapter_suggestions.py, refine.py, summaries.py, video_visual.py, vision.py), plus whisper's generic _emit_ws_event, by routing them through a new unlisted module app/addon_events.py. This changes how events that have nothing to do with processing.updated get delivered.
findings.impact: In production, CORE_INTERNAL_SECRET is set and /api/internal/addon-events rejects any request without the header (backend/app/routers/internal.py:62-65, 731). Before this change, the refine, summaries, vision and whisper emitters posted without the header, so their events were dropped. Now they arrive and are broadcast. Vision's events carry no drive (vision.py:763-808: data is {file_id, model|reason}), so the core broadcasts them with drive=None (internal.py:740) to every connected viewer. That includes viewers who cannot open the file's drive, which breaks the design-decisions rule on the drive boundary for locked drives. Frontend handlers for refine, summary, vision and transcription events, which effectively never fired before, now fire in normal use.
findings.evidence: addons/intelligence/app/addon_events.py (new) adds X-Internal-Secret, trust_env=False and raise_for_status. The old refine.py, summaries.py, vision.py and whisper.py _emit_ws_event bodies sent no secret header, and vision.py sent no top-level drive. The new vision.py:473-476 calls post_addon_event(event, data), and _payload lifts a drive only from data['drive'], which vision never sets. The spec's touch points name only metadata.py, whisper.py (for processing.updated), indexer.py, routers/files.py, the manifest, the messages and the tests.
findings.repro: Read-only. With CORE_INTERNAL_SECRET set, trace one vision event: the old body posted {event, data} with no secret, which verify_internal_secret rejects with 403. The new body posts with the secret, and broadcast is called with drive=None. Not executed.

bucket_proposal.reason: This is outside the declared touch points, and the drive-leak consequence breaks a project design rule (design-decisions: drive boundary) rather than one of I1–I13. I6 covers only processing.updated.

findings.proposed_fix: Either keep the shared helper limited to the processing.updated poster and leave the other workers alone, or add the five workers and addon_events.py to the touch points through a spec revision and make vision events carry drive before they become deliverable.

Addon: routers/files.py, workers/metadata.py, workers/whisper.py, indexer.py, manifest.json, the frontend messages and the tests are listed. addon_events.py, processing_events.py, schemas.py, chapter_suggestions.py, refine.py, summaries.py, video_visual.py and vision.py are not.
potential_unspecified_behavior: Vision, refine, summaries and transcription events now pass the core's secret gate and are broadcast. Vision events without a drive go to every viewer.
chapter_suggestions and video_visual now swallow every exception, where before they caught only httpx.HTTPError.
regression_risks: Frontend listeners for intelligence.* events that were silently dropped in production now receive them, which may surface UI behavior nobody has exercised.
A sync HTTP post (up to 3 s) now runs inside fail_orphaned_running_jobs at startup and inside worker write paths.
test_coverage: test_addon_event_secret.py checks the header and that no module other than the helper posts to addon-events. Nothing checks that drive scoping is preserved for the refactored emitters (vision has no drive).
There is no test for the behavior change of the refine, summaries and vision emitters.
